findings.detail: The current roadmap describes N-120 as Windows junction/reparse GREEN plus QA and review. Its existing node also requires a real native judge rc2 with a typed private precondition, one HMAC-signed event, automatic reviewer dispatch, and safe auto-apply. The roadmap says older done_when remain binding, but its N-120 milestone and close instruction do not make that complete chain an explicit close gate.

The roadmap puts N-120 integration and native node close before N-124 proves the cross-branch ID and PLAN-identity guard. N-124 documents an actual N-120 collision. A clean worktree and manual authority check do not satisfy its fail-closed allocation/close acceptance criterion.

verdict.next: Revise the N-120 milestone to require its full native judge-to-safe-apply chain, and gate N-120 integration/close on N-124’s proven cross-branch identity protection; then repeat semantic plan review. The plan correctly keeps narrow existing native evidence distinct from future E2E, and preserves sealed holdout and release/LPR gates.

open_gates: N-120 full native judge rc2 -> signed receipt -> reviewer -> safe auto-apply
N-124 cross-branch ID protection before N120 integration/close
N-110/N-093/N-073 native autonomy and causal effect
note: Independent DRIFT is a finding to correct, not approval of implementation, release or installation. A new plan SHA needs a new independent review.
